title: axe aria-hidden-focus: focusable recharts SVG inside aria-hidden observer-pie wrapper
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 2.4.3 Focus Order A)
description: axe-core rule `aria-hidden-focus` (impact: serious), 1 instance on the Statistics tab. The decorative observers donut is wrapped in <div aria-hidden="true">, but the recharts <PieChart> renders its SVG with tabIndex=0 (recharts accessibilityLayer default), so keyboard users Tab into an element that screen readers cannot perceive — a focus ghost with no announcement.
fix: Pass accessibilityLayer={false} (or tabIndex={-1}) to this PieChart so the hidden decorative chart is also removed from the tab order. Audit the other aria-hidden chart wrappers for the same recharts default.

verdict.reasoning: recharts 3.8.1 defaults accessibilityLayer to true (PieChart.d.ts) and RootSurface.js then renders the SVG with tabIndex=0 and role=application; the PieChart at BirdingStats.tsx:1287 passes no override and sits directly inside <div aria-hidden="true"> (line 1286). That is exactly axe's aria-hidden-focus (serious): a tab stop screen readers cannot perceive. It is the only aria-hidden chart wrapper in the file, matching the claimed 1 instance; the accessibilityLayer={false} fix is valid for this recharts version.

title: Breeding-tier colored text on 8–15% tier tints fails in both themes (1.97–4.12:1)
description: Active breeding pills set color: var(--sr-tier-N) over rgba(var(--sr-tier-N-rgb), 0.08–0.15) composited on the card surface. Computed over --sr-surface: LIGHT — tier-1 text on tier-1@0.15 = 2.32:1 (any active tier-1 code pill, and the 'Possible' filter pill in BirdingStats); DARK — tier-4 text 1.97:1 (the active 'Confirmed' category pill), tier-3 text 2.94:1, tier-2 text 4.12:1, tier-2-on-tier-1-tint 3.53:1. Same defect at BreedingCodeList.tsx:58-60 (category pills), SpeciesDetail.tsx:786-788 (breeding category pill), BirdingStats.tsx:1637-1638 (Confirmed/Probable/Possible filter pills). Related same-root-cause case: the white badge count on the tier-2 circle (BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219) is 3.96:1 in dark (tier-2 lightened to #A855F7) while passing in light (5.38:1).
fix: Introduce --sr-tier-N-fg tokens per theme for text-on-tint (dark theme needs the text far lighter than the fill tokens; light theme tier-1 needs the existing --sr-tier-1-text dark purple), and extend the tier-1-text pattern to the dark-mode tier-2 badge circle (dark text on #A855F7 would pass).

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran all contrast math independently (alpha-compositing tints over --sr-surface with globals.css token values): every claimed ratio reproduces exactly (light tier-1 2.32:1; dark tier-4 1.97, tier-3 2.94, tier-2 4.12, tier-2-on-tier-1 3.53; badge 3.96 dark / 5.38 light), and pill text is 12px/500 so the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies. The pairs genuinely co-occur in codePillStyle (line 45) and categoryPillStyle (lines 58-60) active states, plus the cited BirdingStats:1626/1637-1638, SpeciesDetail:786-788, and BreedingCodeTable:219 locations, all verified in current code. ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this — it affirmatively claims filter pills meet 4.5:1 in both themes, so 'serious' is the right severity; the suggested --sr-tier-N-fg fix matches the existing --sr-tier-1-text both-themes token precedent and I verified dark #1A0030 on dark tier-2 #A855F7 = 4.88:1 passes.

title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). The same style-only-state defect appears in SpeciesDetail.tsx:1189 (Pins/Heatmap map-mode buttons), BirdingStats.tsx:541 (accumulation granularity), :1628 (breeding filter pills), :1717 (media view mode), ListComparer.tsx:215 (My List / Upload source buttons), and MapExplorer.tsx:1030 (hotspot kind-legend toggles, whose only state cue is opacity 0.4). A screen-reader user cannot tell which option is active. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md: "Filter pills announce whether they are pressed." The codebase already has the correct pattern (SortSeg in Checklists.tsx:74, SnowMap.tsx:144, SpeciesDetail graph groups :962/:974).
fix: Add aria-pressed={value === opt.value} (or role="radio"/aria-checked inside a role="radiogroup") to SegControl's buttons and to each listed location; wrap each group in role="group" with an aria-label.

verdict.reasoning: SegControl (MapSidebarUI.tsx:15-29) renders plain buttons with style-only active state, and every cited usage checks out: MapExplorer 700/881/912/1285, SpeciesDetail ~1189, BirdingStats 541/1628/1717, ListComparer 215, and the hotspot kind-legend toggles at MapExplorer 1030 whose only state cue is opacity 0.4. The correct pattern does exist in SortSeg (Checklists.tsx, role=group + aria-pressed) and SnowMap.tsx:144, and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'filter pills announce whether they are pressed' claim is contradicted rather than disclosed as an exception. Serious is fair: a screen-reader user cannot determine the active option on roughly ten primary filter/view controls.
verdict.fixNote: Give SegControl an ariaLabel prop rendered as role="group" aria-label on its wrapper div plus aria-pressed={value === opt.value} on each button, mirroring SortSeg in Checklists.tsx (the SidebarLabel above it is not programmatically associated, so the group needs its own label). Apply the same aria-pressed to the inline groups in SpeciesDetail, BirdingStats, and ListComparer; for the kind-legend visibility toggles use aria-pressed={!isHidden} so pressed means shown.

title: Species Detail / Named Birds map pins (DOM markers) have no keyboard access path
description: The shared SightingsMap renders each sighting pin as a react-map-gl <Marker> whose content is a plain <div> with a click handler routed through Marker onClick — no tabIndex, no role, no keydown handler — so a keyboard user can never open the per-coordinate popup. On Species Detail ("Sighting Locations" map) that popup is the ONLY place exposing the per-sighting checklist links for sightings without comments (Top Locations rows at SpeciesDetail.tsx:1122-1137 show only name+count; the Comments section only covers commented sightings), so those eBird links are pointer-only functionality. Same pattern, lower impact (keyboard equivalents exist nearby): TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 chip markers (mitigated by the sidebar "Nearest Targets" locate buttons opening the same popup) and BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 geographic-stats rank pins (popup content fully duplicated in the adjacent "Top locations" text lists). Named Birds card maps are also unreachable but each row already lists every sighting's checklist link (NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100). Note ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim covers only the Map Explorer GL markers; these DOM-marker maps have no equivalent of its in-view lists.
fix: DOM markers CAN be focusable (unlike the GL pins): make the marker content a <button aria-label={locName + ' — N sightings'}> so Tab+Enter opens the popup, or reuse the Map Explorer pattern (a focusable list of coordinates that drives the same selectedCoord state). For Species Detail specifically, alternatively surface the per-coordinate checklist links in the keyboard-reachable Top Locations rows.

verdict.reasoning: Verified SightingsMap.tsx:54-58 (and TargetMarkers.tsx, BirdingStats.tsx:862-872): pins are plain div Marker children with click wired through react-map-gl's native click listener; maplibre only adds tabindex/keypress via setPopup(), which this code never uses, so no pin is focusable or keyboard-activatable. The Species Detail impact claim checks out — Top Locations rows (SpeciesDetail.tsx:1115-1138) show name+count only and the Comments section filters to commented sightings (line 372), so checklist links for uncommented sightings are popup-only, i.e. pointer-only. ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim is explicitly Map Explorer-scoped and its only disclosed exception is chart-label contrast, so this Level A lockout is undisclosed; serious is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The button-child fix needs no custom keydown handler: react-map-gl attaches a native click listener to the marker wrapper, so Enter/Space on a real <button aria-label={`${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`}> child dispatches a click that bubbles to it. One refinement: maplibre's Marker.addTo() already stamps the wrapper div with role='button' + generic aria-label='Map marker', so via the Marker ref call marker.getElement().setAttribute('role','presentation') and removeAttribute('aria-label') to avoid a nested-button announcement (or instead set the descriptive aria-label + tabindex on the wrapper itself through the ref and skip the inner button). Apply the same treatment to TargetMarkers.tsx and the BirdingStats rank pins; the Species Detail alternative (links in Top Locations rows) should reuse the existing NamedBirdRow.tsx aria-label pattern for checklist anchors.

title: axe color-contrast: 139 runtime instances in light theme, traceable to ~4 token-level causes
description: axe-core rule `color-contrast` (impact: serious), 139 violating nodes across all 10 tabs at default (light) theme, deduped by failing color pair: (a) --sr-accent #2D8653 (globals.css:29) used as small text fails by a hair on every light surface — 4.32:1 on #f9fafb (active tab label in TabNav, all 10 tabs), 4.03:1 on #e8f5ee accent-bg (selected segmented/sort buttons, 24x), 4.11–4.33:1 on #f4f4f5/#fafafa (links, 9x); (b) --sr-text-muted #71717A (globals.css:18) on --sr-surface-subtle #f4f4f5 = 4.39:1 — the 66 "Jump to section" nav pills (BirdingStats.tsx:450) and similar chips; (c) --sr-text-disabled #A1A1AA (globals.css:19) used for INFORMATIVE text at 2.33–2.56:1 — result-count announcements ("87 comments" aria-live spans in Checklists/LifeList), empty date-input text (color: var(--sr-text-disabled) at SpeciesDetail.tsx:638 etc.), "267 species" counts — worst offenders; (d) chart/inline labels: hardcoded white 10px % labels on --sr-graph-photo #3B82F6 bars = 3.67:1 (BirdingStats.tsx:1153, 5x) and on --sr-graph-video #8B5CF6 = 4.23:1; --sr-tier-1 #C084FC 1.5rem-bold breeding "Possible" count on white = 2.64:1, below even the 3:1 large-text threshold (BirdingStats.tsx:1613); --sr-accent-border-strong text "Loaded from Settings" on accent-bg = 2.52:1 (ListComparer); Settings date-format sublabels 3.16–3.33:1.
fix: Token-level fixes in globals.css :root — darken --sr-accent to ~#277448 (≥4.5 on #f4f4f5) and --sr-text-muted to ~#65656e; stop using --sr-text-disabled for informative text (counts, date values) — switch those to --sr-text-muted; for chart labels either darken the bar fills the white text sits on or move labels outside the bars; use --sr-tier-1 only for swatches, not text, or pair the tier-1 stat with a darker text token.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed every claimed pair and all match within 0.03 (accent 4.32/4.03/4.11/4.33 as small text incl. the 0.875rem/500 TabNav active label; muted 4.40 on the verified jump pills; disabled 2.33-2.56 confirmed on informative text at Checklists.tsx:177/668 aria-live counts, SpeciesDetail.tsx:638, Settings sublabels; white-on-#3B82F6 3.68 at BirdingStats.tsx:1153; tier-1 2.64 at :1613; accent-border-strong 2.53 at ListComparer.tsx:258). ACCESSIBILITY.md discloses only the chart-bar percentage-label subpart and otherwise claims AA for text/buttons/links in both themes, which the accent/muted/disabled items contradict, so not treated as disclosed. Proposed fixes verified: #277448 yields 5.09-5.46 and #65656e yields 5.25 on the cited surfaces; token-level :root changes fit conventions (dark theme has its own values).

title: No h1, most views have no headings, and heading levels are inconsistent across tabs
description: The app title "SnowRaven" is styled <span>s in a <div> (App.tsx:570-580) — no h1 and no banner landmark. Settings, Life List, Species Detail, and Map Explorer contain no heading elements at all (section titles like "Appearance"/"Map Overlays" are styled divs), so SR heading navigation lands on nothing in four major views. Where headings do exist they are inconsistent: ListComparer.tsx:184 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:340 use h1 inside tab content while Checklists.tsx:522, BirdingStats.tsx:424 and NamedBirds.tsx:128 use h2; SetupRequired.tsx:31 (the empty state of 8 tabs) styles its title as a div. Additionally the main nav loses its landmark: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides the navigation role, and in dropdown mode there is no nav element at all.
fix: Make the app title an h1 inside a <header>; give every tab view an h2 and section cards h3 (Settings/LifeList/SpeciesDetail/MapExplorer sidebar sections); make SetupRequired's title an h2; demote the comparer h1s to h2.

verdict.reasoning: All claims check out: the title is styled spans in a div (App.tsx:570-580, no h1/header element); grep shows zero heading elements in Settings, LifeList, SpeciesDetail, MapExplorer and SetupRequired (title is a styled div, SetupRequired.tsx:31); ListComparer:184/ChecklistComparer:340 use h1 in tab content while Checklists:522/BirdingStats:424/NamedBirds:128 use h2; TabNav.tsx:105-108 puts role="tablist" on the <nav> (killing the navigation landmark) and the dropdown variant renders no nav at all. Heading navigation is a primary SR strategy and four major views expose nothing, so this is genuinely user-impacting at 1.3.1 Level A; moderate is the right tier since tablist/main/contentinfo landmarks still give a navigation path.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested heading plan is sound (h1 title in <header>, h2 per view incl. SetupRequired, h3 section cards — statsPrimitives.tsx already uses h3 for stats cards, so follow that pattern), but it omits the landmark half of its own description: also move role="tablist" off the <nav> in TabNav.tsx onto an inner div so the navigation landmark survives, and wrap the dropdown-mode trigger+listbox in the same <nav aria-label="Main navigation">.

title: In-page jump links scroll the view but never move keyboard focus
description: The Statistics "Jump to section" nav (9 anchors) calls e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and LifeList's "media comments" anchor does the same (LifeList.tsx:505). preventDefault suppresses the browser's native sequential-focus relocation for fragment navigation, and the scroll targets are plain divs without tabindex="-1" (e.g. MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40), so after "jumping" a keyboard user's focus is still on the link at the top — the next Tab continues from the nav and they must traverse every control between anyway. The jump feature is effectively visual-only for keyboard users.
fix: After scrolling, move focus to the destination: give each section container tabindex={-1} and call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }) alongside smoothScrollIntoView (wrap in the existing scroll helper so all jump links inherit it).

verdict.reasoning: BirdingStats.tsx:449 (and LifeList.tsx:505) call e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and lib/scroll.ts only scrolls — it never moves focus; the targets are plain divs (SectionCard in statsPrimitives.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40) with no tabindex. preventDefault suppresses the browser's native fragment-navigation focus relocation, so after a jump the next Tab resumes from the nav chip — the feature is visual-only for keyboard users. The suggested fix (tabindex=-1 on targets + focus({preventScroll:true}) folded into the shared scroll helper) is correct and convention-conforming.
verdict.fixNote: Put tabIndex={-1} on the SectionCard root div (statsPrimitives.tsx) so all nine Statistics targets inherit it, add the same to the #media-comments div in MediaCommentsSection.tsx, and add a jumpTo(el) wrapper in lib/scroll.ts that calls smoothScrollIntoView(el) then el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); switch the three preventDefault call sites (BirdingStats.tsx:449, LifeList.tsx:505) to it. Add :focus-visible-only outline styling (or outline: none on [tabindex="-1"]) so the programmatic focus doesn't paint the green focus ring on the whole card for mouse users.

title: Chart hover tooltips are not hoverable (1.4.13): cursor-following wrapper with pointer-events none on all five recharts Tooltip mounts
wcag: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus AA (failure F95 — content on hover not hoverable)
description: All five recharts <Tooltip> mounts — BirdingStats.tsx:575 and :601 (life-list accumulation area charts), :1276 (checklists-by-observer bar chart), :1768 (media-over-time line chart), and MediaStatsSections.tsx:320 (media-by-hour stacked bar chart) — pass only contentStyle/formatter/labelFormatter, so recharts 3.8.1 defaults apply (trigger 'hover', no fixed position, no wrapperStyle). The library renders the tooltip in a wrapper hardcoded to pointerEvents:'none' that follows the cursor at a ~10px offset (node_modules/recharts/es6/component/TooltipBoundingBox.js:77), so the pointer can never be moved over the tooltip content: approaching it repositions the box and swaps its data to a different point, and at the plot edge the move exits the hover area and the tooltip vanishes. That fails 1.4.13's hoverable condition, which exists for screen-magnification users who must bring revealed content under the lens to read it — the media chart's five-line tooltip in particular can extend past a 400% lens and cannot be panned to without the content changing. The other two 1.4.13 conditions PASS in this recharts version (verified in installed source, see passes), which bounds the severity, as does the trigger-adjacent placement; and because every chart wrapper is role="img" with an aria-label summary, this is a sighted-pointer-user issue only (per-point values are otherwise unavailable as visible text anywhere in the UI). The tooltip is also clamped inside the chart viewBox (allowEscapeViewBox default false), so it can overlay bars, axis ticks, and the media chart's in-container legend — acceptable under 1.4.13 only because the Escape dismissal works. ACCESSIBILITY.md makes no claim about hover content, so this is an undisclosed gap rather than a false statement.
evidence: BirdingStats.tsx:575-582/:601-605/:1276-1280/:1768-1773 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:320-323 pass no content/trigger/position/wrapperStyle props; recharts 3.8.1 TooltipBoundingBox.js:77 sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` in positionStyle and translates the box from the live cursor coordinate via getTooltipTranslate; defaultTooltipProps in Tooltip.js:36-58 sets `trigger: 'hover'`.
suggestedFix: Pick one per-chart approach and apply it to all five mounts: (a) anchor the tooltip with a fixed `position={{ x, y }}` (e.g. a chart corner) plus `wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }}` — wrapperStyle is spread after the hardcoded style so it wins — making the box stationary and physically hoverable; or (b) switch to `trigger="click"` (supported in recharts 3), which makes the content activation-triggered and exempt from 1.4.13 entirely, matching the posture the app already takes for map popups; or (c) surface the per-point values in a visible-text alternative (a small data-table disclosure under each chart). Mention chart tooltips in ACCESSIBILITY.md once fixed.

verdict.reasoning: All five Tooltip mounts (BirdingStats.tsx:575/601/1276/1768, MediaStatsSections.tsx:320) pass only contentStyle/formatter/labelFormatter, and the installed recharts 3.8.1 hardcodes pointerEvents:'none' plus cursor-following translate in TooltipBoundingBox.js and trigger:'hover' in defaultTooltipProps — so the hover content can never be hovered, an F95 failure of 1.4.13. The bounding claims also check out: Escape dismissal exists in TooltipBoundingBox, every chart wrapper is role=img with an aria-label, and wrapperStyle is spread after the hardcoded positionStyle so fix option (a) works. No existing finding covers 1.4.13/chart tooltips and ACCESSIBILITY.md says nothing about hover content.
verdict.fixNote: Option (a) is verified workable in the installed source: outerStyle = {...positionStyle, visibility..., ...props.wrapperStyle}, so wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }} wins, but it only satisfies 1.4.13 combined with a fixed position prop (otherwise the box still tracks the cursor). Option (b) trigger="click" is the lowest-risk route and matches the app's map-popup posture.

title: Hardcoded milestone-chip and rank-icon colors below AA (2.76–4.16:1), bypassing the token system
description: The Firsts & Milestones chips hardcode hex colors (also violating the project's tokens-only rule): the tier-1 date link #5EA07C on #E8F5EE = 2.76:1 (10px text), tier-1 number #2D8653 on #E8F5EE = 4.03:1, tier-2 date #3E7A56 on #D8EDE4 = 4.16:1 (tier-3/4 pass: 4.92–6.37:1). These values are identical in both themes since the chips don't adapt. Separately, RankIcon (statsPrimitives.tsx:97-98) prints white 10px-bold rank numbers on hardcoded #3B82F6 = 3.68:1 (the #2D8653 circle squeaks by at 4.52:1).
fix: Move the milestone palette into --sr-* tokens and darken the failing fg values (date ≥ #43755C on #E8F5EE; num → --sr-accent-strong); for RankIcon use --sr-chart-blue-dark (#1D4ED8, 6.70:1 under white) as the square fill.

verdict.reasoning: Hardcoded hexes verified at BirdingStats.tsx:671-677 and statsPrimitives.tsx:95-98 (violating the CLAUDE.md tokens-only rule), and my recomputation matches: tier-1 date 2.76:1 and tier-2 date 4.16:1 at 10px (need 4.5), RankIcon white-on-#3B82F6 3.68:1 at 10px bold (need 4.5). One overstatement: the tier-1 threshold number is 1.25rem/700 = 20px bold = WCAG large text, so its 4.03:1 PASSES at the 3:1 large-text threshold — the real failures are the two date links and the RankIcon square. Still a fair moderate: real sub-AA text plus a standing-convention violation.
verdict.fixNote: Tokenize the milestone palette into --sr-milestone-* tokens defined in BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] (globals.css), darkening only the failing date colors (tier-1 date >= #43755C on #E8F5EE = 4.76:1, tier-2 date similarly); the tier-1 number (20px bold = large text) already passes at 4.03:1 >= 3:1 and needs no change. Do NOT use var(--sr-chart-blue-dark) for the RankIcon square as suggested — it resolves to #3B82F6 in the dark theme, which is 3.68:1 under the white 10px-bold rank text and still fails; instead add a dedicated token (e.g. --sr-rank-square: #1D4ED8 in both themes, 6.70:1 under white) and use var(--sr-accent... ) tokens for the circle.

title: Disclosed chart-bar-label exception verified — but it understates the dark-theme failures (down to 1.29:1) and a working fix already exists in-code
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md's known exception ('a few dense data-visualization labels (percentage figures printed inside saturated chart bars) do not yet meet AA in every case') is accurate in direction but materially understates scope. Computed: LIGHT — white on --sr-graph-audio 2.15:1 (protocol bar), white on --sr-chart-slate 2.56:1, white on --sr-graph-photo 3.68:1, white on --sr-graph-video 4.23:1. DARK — --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light 1.29:1 (comment/species-notes bars, BirdingStats.tsx:1384/1405), white on graph-audio 1.44:1, white on --sr-accent 1.92:1 (hardcoded '#fff' at protocol bar :1181), white on graph-photo 2.54:1, white on chart-slate 2.56:1, --sr-text on chart-slate 2.33:1 (:1361), white on chart-blue-dark 3.68:1 (:1125). In dark mode it is most in-bar labels, not 'a few'. Notably, line 1358 already uses var(--sr-on-accent) which passes in BOTH themes (4.52/7.75) — the failures are the literal '#fff' and var(--sr-text) usages that don't adapt.
fix: Replace literal '#fff' bar-label colors with per-fill adaptive tokens (the existing --sr-on-accent pattern), or render the percentage outside/beside the segment when the segment color can't carry AA text; then tighten the ACCESSIBILITY.md wording to match whatever remains.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed every cited pair with my own WCAG relative-luminance implementation; all match (dark --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light = 1.29:1 at lines 1384/1405, white on dark graph-audio 1.44, white on dark accent 1.92 via the hardcoded '#fff' at 1181, dark text-on-slate 2.33 at 1361, white on dark chart-blue-dark 3.68 at 1125), and line 1358's --sr-on-accent does pass both themes (4.52/7.75) proving the fix pattern exists in-code. Labels are 11-12px weight-600, so the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies — in dark mode most in-bar labels fail, some catastrophically, which materially exceeds the 'a few cases' wording in ACCESSIBILITY.md line 31. Confirmed at moderate: the percentages are supplemental (raw counts appear in the adjacent header text), but 1.29:1 is effectively invisible text.

title: Repeated "↗" checklist links named only by the arrow glyph
wcag: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) A / 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA
description: Three Statistics sections render external eBird checklist links whose only content is the character "↗" with title="Open checklist": the effort superlative cards (line 1332), single-checklist-bird chips (line 1564), and one-and-done bird chips (line 1589). The accessible name is computed from content, so every one of these (potentially dozens in the chip lists) is announced as "north east arrow, link" or skipped entirely depending on SR symbol verbosity — identical and non-descriptive. title only provides a description, not the name, when content exists.
fix: Add aria-label, e.g. aria-label={`Open eBird checklist ${bird.submissionId} for ${bird.name} (opens in a new tab)`}, mirroring NamedBirdRow.tsx:94 which already does this correctly, and mark the glyph aria-hidden.

verdict.reasoning: All three sites verified (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589): anchor content is solely the ↗ character with title="Open checklist", so per accname computation the name is the glyph (title only supplies the description when content exists) — dozens of identical, non-descriptive links in the chip lists, indistinguishable in a screen-reader links list. The cited in-repo precedent is real: NamedBirdRow.tsx:94 already uses aria-label={`Open eBird checklist ${s.submissionId} (opens in a new tab)`} with an aria-hidden icon. Moderate is fair (2.4.4 in-context is arguable for the chip-adjacent bird name, but the repeated-identical-name failure mode is genuine) and the suggested fix matches the codebase pattern exactly.

title: Map popups cannot be dismissed with the keyboard (no close button, no Escape)
description: Every app-rendered map popup passes closeButton={false}, and MapLibre's Popup has no built-in Escape handling (verified: no keydown/Escape in maplibre-gl/src/ui/popup.ts), so the only dismissal is a pointer click on empty map. The Map Explorer in-view list rows open popups by keyboard (good) but never close them: onActivate always sets the locId (MapExplorer.tsx:504-512) — re-activating a row with aria-pressed="true" does not toggle it off, so the pressed state is also a one-way lie. Affected popups: SightingMarkers.tsx:111, HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. A stuck-open popup overlays the map and inserts extra tab stops (eBird links inside it). The AtlasLayer popup (AtlasLayer.tsx:205) is the one that keeps the default close button — proving the styled close button is available.
fix: Either re-enable closeButton (MapLibre renders a real <button aria-label="Close popup">, already themed via .maplibregl-popup-content CSS), or add an Escape keydown handler that clears the selection state, and make in-view list rows toggle (activating the already-selected row calls onSelect(null)). Any one of these resolves it; the row toggle also fixes the aria-pressed semantics.

verdict.reasoning: All five cited popups pass closeButton={false} at the exact lines, maplibre-gl's bundle contains zero Escape handling, and MapExplorer's only Escape handler is the mobile-sidebar focus trap — so popups opened via the keyboard-accessible in-view lists (which one-way set locId, never toggling aria-pressed rows off) have no keyboard dismissal at all. The HotspotMarkers popup adds real eBird-link tab stops, making this user-impacting under WCAG 2.1.1. ACCESSIBILITY.md describes the keyboard open path but does not disclose the missing dismissal; the suggested fix is accurate and convention-aligned (AtlasLayer.tsx:205 keeps the default close button, a real <button aria-label="Close popup"> already themed via .maplibregl-popup-close-button with var(--sr-text-muted) in globals.css:576).

title: DOM map markers (Species Detail / Named Birds pins, target chips, Statistics rank pins) are unnamed, role-less click targets invisible to AT
wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content A / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md documents sidebar-list alternatives for the Map Explorer's GPU canvas markers, but the DOM <Marker> maps have no equivalent treatment: SightingsMap.tsx:55-58 renders each pin as a clickable <div> containing an innerHTML SVG with no role, name, or tabindex; TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 does the same for target chips; BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 for the Statistics RankIcon pins (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101, an unnamed SVG). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or activate any of these markers or reach their popups. Impact is moderated because equivalent data exists in adjacent text on most surfaces (Named Birds rows list every sighting date/location/checklist; Species Detail has Top Locations and per-sighting lists; Statistics has top-location tables), but the popup-only details (e.g. per-coordinate date groupings) have no named path.
fix: Make the Marker child a real button: role="button", tabIndex=0, aria-label like `${locName ?? coordinate}, ${sightings.length} sightings` with Enter/Space handling — or explicitly scope the ACCESSIBILITY.md marker claim and guarantee a text equivalent exists beside every DOM-marker map.

verdict.reasoning: The literal 'no role, name' claim is partly wrong — maplibre 5.24's Marker.addTo() (src/ui/marker.ts:340-348) stamps every marker wrapper with role='button' and default aria-label='Map marker' — but the substantive 1.1.1 failure stands: all pins announce identically with no location/count, are not focusable (tabindex comes only from the unused setPopup path), and the popup-only per-coordinate details have no named path. The cited mitigations are real (BirdingStats pins duplicate the adjacent 'Top locations by checklists/species' lists; NamedBirdRow lists every checklist link; TargetMarkers has the Nearest Targets sidebar), so moderate is the right severity. ACCESSIBILITY.md's marker claim is Map Explorer-only and does not disclose this.
verdict.fixNote: Correction to the finding's mechanism: the markers are not role-less/invisible — maplibre already applies role='button' + a generic identical aria-label ('Map marker') to the wrapper, so the defect is a non-descriptive name plus no focusability. Fix by giving each pin a descriptive per-pin name: either set it on the wrapper via the Marker ref (marker.getElement().setAttribute('aria-label', `${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`) plus tabindex='0' — maplibre preserves a pre-set label), or render a real <button aria-label=...> child and demote the wrapper to role='presentation' via the ref to avoid nested-button announcements. The finding's hand-rolled role='button'/tabIndex/Enter-Space div is workable but creates button-inside-button nesting and re-implements what a native <button> gives for free.

title: Fixed-pixel text geometry in Statistics overlaps or clips at 200% text scale (pattern, multiple locations)
wcag: 1.4.4 Resize Text AA (clipping cases also 1.4.12 Text Spacing AA)
description: One repeating pattern: rem-sized text placed in fixed-pixel boxes that don't grow with the text. (1) BarRow (statsPrimitives.tsx:59-75): label column `width: labelWidth, flexShrink: 0` and value column `width: pctOf ? 68 : 40`, no overflow handling — at 200% scale, labels ("Jan" at labelWidth=28: BirdingStats.tsx:754,794,829; "SnowRaven weather" at 120: BirdingStats.tsx:1425-1429; MediaStatsSections.tsx:180-182,294) and values like "1,234 (56%)" are ~2× wider than their boxes and overlap the adjacent bar graphic. (2) Stacked-bar % labels inside fixed-height `overflow: hidden` segments — BirdingStats.tsx:1122-1133 and 1173-1185 (height 32, fits 200%) but the protocol sub-bars at 1151-1158 are `height: 20` with 0.625rem labels: at 200% the 20px glyphs (30px line box) clip vertically; same construction in the media bars at 1356, 1380, 1401. (3) Hard-ellipsized name columns `width: 100`/`width: 96` + nowrap+hidden (BirdingStats.tsx:953, 984, 1028, 1057) — county/species names truncate to a few characters at 200% with only a mouse-only `title` as recovery. (4) Donut center captions absolutely centered in fixed 120/132px charts — BirdingStats.tsx:764-769, 804-807 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:58-61 — at 200% the caption (e.g. "September" ≈140px wide, or a 1.25rem count) spills across the donut ring on both sides. Screen-reader users are unaffected (the role="img" aria-labels carry the data); this degrades the visual rendering for sighted low-vision users at 150-200%.
fix: Convert the fixed widths to rem (e.g. labelWidth 28→'2.5rem', value column '4.5rem') or `minWidth` + `flex-basis`; change the sub-bar `height: 20` to `minHeight: 20` (the % label centers itself, the bar just grows); for the donut captions either size the chart in rem or cap centerValue/centerLabel with a clamp().

verdict.reasoning: All four cited sub-patterns exist in current code (BarRow px label/value columns at statsPrimitives.tsx:59-75 with labelWidth 28/48/120/150 at the cited consumer lines; height-20 overflow-hidden sub-bars at BirdingStats.tsx:1151-1158; 100/96px ellipsized county/state columns at 953/984/1028/1057, counties lacking even a title; fixed 120/132px donut charts with absolutely-centered captions). The app's Text Size control doubles the root font-size via --sr-text-scale while these px boxes stay fixed, so single-word labels overlap the bars, sub-bar labels clip at the 20px clip edge, names truncate to a few characters, and donut captions spill across the ring at 200% — and ACCESSIBILITY.md affirmatively claims 1.4.4 is met 'without clipping content', so this contradicts the published statement rather than being disclosed. Two specifics are overstated (the '1,234 (56%)' values wrap onto a second line rather than overlapping since rows use minHeight, and the height-32 media bars at 1356/1380/1401 fit at 200%), but the pattern and moderate severity stand.
verdict.fixNote: Direction is right, but: BarRow's labelWidth prop is typed `number`, so convert inside the component (width: `${labelWidth / 16}rem`, value column `pctOf ? '4.25rem' : '2.5rem'`) so no call sites change; `height: 20` → `minHeight: 20` on the sub-bars is correct as suggested; recharts PieChart width/height are px numbers so the donut can't be 'sized in rem' — instead give the centered caption maxWidth: '100%' with padding and ellipsis/wrap (or compute the chart px size from the live root font-size); and for the county columns at BirdingStats.tsx:953/984 either add the missing title attribute or replace the hard ellipsis with a rem minWidth that lets names wrap.

title: The same 'open this checklist on eBird' function is identified four different ways across tabs
description: One repeated function — a link that opens a specific checklist on ebird.org — is identified with four different affordances and three different name vocabularies depending on the tab (this is the identification inconsistency itself, distinct from the already-reported missing new-window indication and the ↗ accessible-name weakness): (1) bare '↗' glyph with title="Open checklist" (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589); (2) data value + lucide ExternalLink icon, no label at all (speciesDetail/ui.tsx:52-78 StatValueLink, Checklists.tsx:48-65 DateLink) — except NamedBirdRow.tsx:91-100, where the identical id+icon link carries aria-label="Open eBird checklist S… (opens in a new tab)"; (3) plain accent-colored text with no icon and no underline, indistinguishable from the adjacent non-link values (BirdingStats.tsx:500, 695, 726, 1448, 1525; SightingsMap.tsx:67 popup dates; map/TargetMarkers.tsx:104); (4) underlined id text with title="View this checklist on eBird" (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). Where a name exists it is inconsistent F31-style: "Open checklist" vs "View this checklist on eBird" vs "Open eBird checklist S…". A screen-reader user who learns one identification on the Checklists tab cannot recognize the same function on Statistics or in a map popup, and sighted users get no stable visual signature for 'this opens the checklist' either.
evidence: WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111 `{id}` vs BirdingStats.tsx:1332 `↗` vs Checklists.tsx:54-62 `{formatDate(date)}` (no label) vs BirdingStats.tsx:500-505 date-only link with `textDecoration: 'none'` and no icon.
suggestedFix: Create one shared ChecklistLink component (extending the existing speciesDetail/ui.tsx StatValueLink, which already gates on SUBMISSION_ID_RE) with a single visual signature (ExternalLink icon) and one accessible-name formula (e.g. aria-label=`Open checklist ${id} on eBird` plus the new-tab suffix already used in NamedBirdRow). Replace all four variants — the ↗ glyphs, the unlabeled icon links, the plain-text links, and the title-only underlined ids — with it.

verdict.reasoning: All four variants verified at the cited lines: bare ↗ with title='Open checklist' (BirdingStats 1332/1564/1589), value+ExternalLink with no label (StatValueLink ui.tsx:52-78, DateLink Checklists.tsx:48-65) vs NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100's full aria-label, plain accent text with textDecoration:'none' (BirdingStats 500/695/726/1448/1525, SightingsMap.tsx:62-75, TargetMarkers.tsx:104 — which is in fact a fifth vocabulary, 'View checklist S… →'), and underlined id with title='View this checklist on eBird' (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). This is a genuine 3.2.4 inconsistent-identification issue whose root cause (no shared component or name formula) is distinct from confirmed #53 (↗ missing accessible name) and structure findings #4/#5 (new-window indication, title-attribute reliance), which the finding explicitly carves out. The suggested shared ChecklistLink keeps the SUBMISSION_ID_RE standing security check, consistent with conventions.

title: Bare "↗" glyph checklist links rely on title attribute alone; footer "SnowRaven" link hides its GitHub destination
description: Two weak link-purpose patterns (merged): (1) BirdingStats Highlights/Records links render the single glyph "↗" as their only content with title="Open checklist" (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589). The accessible name comes only from the title fallback — fragile across AT, invisible to sighted keyboard users (title tooltips don't appear on focus), unavailable on touch — and the repeated identical name "Open checklist" is distinguished only by surrounding card/row context. (2) The footer link whose text is "SnowRaven" (App.tsx:1101-1110) actually navigates to the GitHub repository; neither the link text nor its programmatic context ("SnowRaven · Self-hosted Birding Tools") reveals that destination.
evidence: BirdingStats.tsx:1332 `↗`; App.tsx:1101-1109 `SnowRaven`.
suggestedFix: Give the ↗ links a real accessible name including their distinguishing context, e.g. aria-label={`Open ${card.label} checklist on eBird`} (keep title for sighted hover if desired); change the footer link text or aria-label to "SnowRaven on GitHub".

verdict.reasoning: This is a merged finding: part (1) — the bare ↗ checklist links in BirdingStats (verified at 1332, 1564, 1589, title="Open checklist" only) — is a duplicate of confirmed finding #53 (same elements, same root cause: inadequate accessible naming of the repeated ↗ links). Part (2) is real and distinct: App.tsx:1101-1110 footer link with text 'SnowRaven' navigates to the GitHub repo with nothing in the text or contentinfo context revealing the destination, while App.tsx:898 already demonstrates the correct pattern for the SnowRaven Mini link. Confirmed on the footer-link aspect only; minor severity fits a single ambiguous 2.4.4 link.
verdict.fixNote: Treat the ↗-naming portion as covered by confirmed #53 and fix only the footer here: give the footer anchor aria-label="SnowRaven on GitHub (opens in new tab)" (or change the visible text), matching the existing SnowRaven Mini pattern at App.tsx:898.

title: Multi-series line charts differentiated by hue alone
description: The media-over-time chart draws four lines (photo/audio/video/total) distinguished only by stroke color, with a color-keyed legend — for color-blind users the photo (blue) vs video (purple) pair in particular is hard to separate. Tooltips name each series on hover and the role="img" summary covers AT users, so the information is reachable, but not glanceable. Same pattern wherever SightingsGraph's media chart overlays multiple series.
fix: Add per-series strokeDasharray patterns and/or distinct dot marker shapes to the recharts <Line> elements so series differ by more than hue.

verdict.reasoning: Lines 1775-1778 of BirdingStats.tsx render four <Line> series with dot={false}, no strokeDasharray, and only stroke color differentiating them; Vienot protan/deutan simulation collapses the photo #3B82F6 / video #8B5CF6 pair from RGB distance 88.6 to ~1-2 (same in dark theme #60A5FA/#A78BFA), confirming the confusion claim. SightingsGraph.tsx's media overlay (lines ~157-172) is likewise hue-only (its dots are same-shape circles in the series color). Hover tooltips and the role=img label keep the info reachable, so minor severity is correctly stated.
verdict.fixNote: Add per-series strokeDasharray to the four <Line>s in BirdingStats.tsx (e.g. photo solid, audio '6 3', video '2 3', total '8 3 2 3'); since dot={false} there, dashes are the practical cue. Apply the same patterns to the photo/audio/video overlay in speciesDetail/SightingsGraph.tsx (~lines 157-172). Note recharts' default Legend line icon does not render the dash pattern, so either pass a custom legend `content` or distinct `legendType` icons so the legend also differs by more than hue. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md currently claims 'Color is never the only way information is conveyed' — update it (or fix the charts in the same change) per the CLAUDE.md rule that it must stay true.

title: Chart non-text elements below 3:1: amber line in light theme, faint bar segments, stacked-segment boundaries
description: Computed non-text chart parts under 3:1 — light theme: the Audio series line --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs the white card = 2.15:1 (media-over-time chart; SightingsGraph media line too), --sr-chart-blue-light bar segment vs surface = 1.80:1, tier-1 fill vs surface = 2.64:1; the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments: tier-2 vs tier-1 = 2.04:1 light / 1.50:1 dark, tier-4 vs tier-2 = 2.79:1 light / 2.20:1 dark (BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679). Mitigations keeping this minor: every chart has a data-bearing role="img" label, tooltips, and most values are duplicated as text (legend counts, BarRow numerals).
fix: Darken light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1 — already proven in --sr-age-immature), add 1px separators between stacked-bar segments, and bump light --sr-chart-blue-light/tier-1 fills toward their 3:1 neighbors.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited non-text ratios and they match: light --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs white 2.15:1 (media LineChart at :1776), --sr-chart-blue-light vs white 1.80:1, tier-1 vs white 2.64:1, and the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments at :1677-1679 (tier-2/tier-1 2.04 light / 1.50 dark; tier-4/tier-2 2.79 / 2.20). The stated mitigations are real (role="img" summaries at :557/:1266/:1755, legends, BarRow prints value+pct as text), which correctly keeps this at minor under 1.4.11's redundant-presentation allowance — the amber series line is the strongest genuine instance since the lines themselves carry the trend.
verdict.fixNote: Darkening light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1, matches light --sr-age-immature) is verified and safe. But do NOT shift the shared --sr-tier-* palette to fix the stacked-bar boundaries — those tokens drive the map atlas overlay, hatch sprites (--sr-tier-N-rgb), legend parity, and the breeding-badge dark-text-on-light-tier pairing called out in ACCESSIBILITY.md; instead add 1px var(--sr-surface) gaps between the three stacked segments at BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679, which fixes segment distinguishability with zero blast radius.

title: The 'loading-saved' phase on four data tabs is a bare unlabeled spinner — nothing is announced and nothing names the state
wcag: 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (also 1.1.1 Non-text Content A)
description: While a tab parses the stored CSV (the phase every visit passes through before the data or the SetupRequired panel appears), four tabs replace their entire panel with a centered Loader2 SVG and nothing else: Checklists.tsx:468-470 (the icon is even explicitly aria-hidden, leaving zero accessible content in the panel), LifeList.tsx:362-364, SpeciesDetail.tsx:408-410, and BreedingCodeList.tsx:174-176. There is no role="status", no aria-label, and no visible text, so a screen-reader user lands in an empty tabpanel with no indication anything is happening. Every other loading state in the app does this correctly and was recorded as a pass (boot skeleton role=status 'Loading SnowRaven', App.tsx TabLoading role=status with text, BirdingStats.tsx:464 computing status, SnowMap style placeholder) — these four bare spinners are the stragglers. Distinct from prior finding i=74 (which covers role=status nodes that mount with text already present — these have no status semantics at all).
evidence: Checklists.tsx:469 `<Loader2 size={24} strokeWidth={2} className="spin" style={{ color: 'var(--sr-accent)' }} aria-hidden />` as the sole child of the phase's wrapper div; identical Loader2-only blocks at LifeList.tsx:363, SpeciesDetail.tsx:409, BreedingCodeList.tsx:~176 (those three without even aria-hidden, but with no text either).
suggestedFix: Give each wrapper div role="status" and an aria-label (e.g. 'Loading saved eBird data') — or add visible text next to the spinner as WeatherTidePanel does ('Loading weather…') — and keep the SVG aria-hidden, matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern.

verdict.reasoning: All four cited blocks verified: Checklists.tsx:466-472 (Loader2 with aria-hidden as the panel's sole content), LifeList.tsx:360-366, SpeciesDetail.tsx:406-412, BreedingCodeList.tsx:172-178 — no role='status', no aria-label, no text, leaving an empty tabpanel during the loading-saved phase every visit passes through. Genuinely distinct from confirmed i=74, which covers nodes that already have role='status' but mount with text present; these have no status semantics at all. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md and not present in either findings file.
verdict.fixNote: Matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern (role='status' + label on the wrapper, SVG aria-hidden) is right; note per confirmed finding i=74 that a status node mounting with its label may still not be announced by all SRs, but it at least names the state for users who land in the panel — fixing both together would mean mounting the empty status container first and inserting the label.

title: External links open new windows without any indication (inconsistent across the app)
description: 43 target="_blank" anchors exist across ~20 component files; only two indicate the behavior — App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 use "(opens in new tab)" in aria-label. All others give no warning, including every link in the Help documentation (HelpDocs.tsx:61 renders all HELP.md links with target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" and no indication), the footer GitHub link (App.tsx:1101-1110), SpeciesLinks.tsx:20/45 (whose aria-labels "View X on eBird" omit it), LifeListTable.tsx media-count links, BirdingStats.tsx checklist/region links (15 instances), Checklists.tsx, MapExplorer.tsx, SpeciesDetail.tsx, NamedBirdRow.tsx, Settings.tsx, WeatherTidePanel.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx, MediaStatsSections.tsx, ChecklistComparer.tsx, SightingsMap.tsx, map/HotspotMarkers.tsx, map/TargetMarkers.tsx, AtlasLayer.tsx, speciesDetail/ui.tsx, CommentText.tsx. Unexpected context changes disorient screen-reader and cognitive-disability users; the app already has the right pattern in two places — it just isn't applied consistently.
evidence: HelpDocs.tsx:61 `<a key={ki++} href={lm[2]} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` with no new-window indication; grep shows 43 target="_blank" instances, only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 carry "(opens in new tab)".
suggestedFix: Adopt one shared ExternalA component (or extend SpeciesLinks' pattern) that appends "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name (visually-hidden span or aria-label suffix) and use it for all target="_blank" anchors, including HelpDocs' renderInline link branch.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by grep: exactly 43 target="_blank" anchors across 20 component files, with only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 announcing '(opens in new tab)'; HelpDocs.tsx renders every documentation link target="_blank" with no indication and SpeciesLinks.tsx aria-labels omit it. This is the new-window-indication aspect, explicitly distinct from confirmed #53 (which covers the ↗ links' accessible names), so not a duplicate. Correctly scoped as advisory (G201; 3.2.5 is AAA), so minor severity is right; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: A shared external-link component is sound; prefer a visually-hidden span suffix over aria-label so existing link text is preserved, and where an aria-label already exists (SpeciesLinks, icon-only links) append to the label, matching the wording already used at App.tsx:748/898. For icon-only favicon links keep title in sync with the label.

title: Statistics map rank-pin numerals are fixed 10px SVG text — only text in the app that ignores the Text Size control
description: RankIcon renders a fixed 24×24 SVG with `fontSize="10"` for the rank numbers on the Statistics geographic map pins (BirdingStats.tsx:865, 871). The numeral does not scale with the Text Size control or OS text size. Mitigations: it is map content (markers on a map get latitude under 1.4.10/1.4.4), and the same ranking is available as scalable text in the "Top locations by checklists/species" lists directly below (BirdingStats.tsx:906, 921). Reported as polish, plus a note: the icon fills are hardcoded hex (`#2D8653`, `#3B82F6`, echoed in the legend swatches at BirdingStats.tsx:888/892 and the popup gray `#71717A` at :876), which violates the project's own --sr-* token rule.
fix: Size the SVG in em (width/height '1.5em') so the pin and numeral track the root scale, or accept as map content and document it; swap the hardcoded hexes for var(--sr-*) tokens while there.

verdict.reasoning: RankIcon (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101) is exactly as described — fixed 24x24 SVG with fontSize="10" numerals used as map Markers at BirdingStats.tsx:865/871, and a grep confirms it is the only SVG <text> in the app, so the numerals are the one text surface that ignores the Text Size control. The stated mitigations hold (the identical ranks render as scalable HTML text in the lists at BirdingStats.tsx:904-925, and map markers get 1.4.10/1.4.4 latitude), so minor/polish is the right severity; the bundled token complaint is also real — #2D8653/#3B82F6/#71717A are hardcoded against CLAUDE.md's explicit 'no hardcoded hex in component files' rule. The popup gray is worse than stylistic: the MapLibre popup background is themed (var(--sr-surface) = #18181B dark), and I computed #71717A on it at 3.67:1, below AA, while var(--sr-text-muted) is #A1A1AA in dark theme precisely for this.
verdict.fixNote: Em-sizing the SVG works (DOM markers inherit the scaled root font-size; note pins double in footprint at 200% and overlap more — acceptable). But do NOT blind-swap the pin fills to var(--sr-accent)/var(--sr-graph-photo): those tokens lighten in dark theme (#34D399/#60A5FA) and the white numeral would drop well below AA, while the pins sit on theme-independent map tiles where the current dark fills are correct in both themes — mint dedicated --sr-rank-pin-circle/--sr-rank-pin-square tokens in BOTH :root and [data-theme=dark] (same dark values in each is fine) and use them for both RankIcon and the legend swatches at BirdingStats.tsx:888/892. The popup gray at :876 should become var(--sr-text-muted) — that one is a real dark-theme AA fix (3.67:1 today), not just hygiene.
